source_text: I. Et nobis est apud vos certamen, dilectissimi fratres, ut nihil aliud agendum dei servis et Christo eius dicatis, quam de multitudine fratrum cogitare; qua vi, qua ratione hic amor, hoc officium ad has nos impulit litteras, ut fratribus post futuris et magnificentiae dei fidele testimonium et labores ac tolerantiam nostri pro domino memoriae relinqueremus. II. Post popularem tumultum quem ferox vultus praesidis in necem concitavit, postque sequentis diei acerrimam persecutionem Christianorum, praevaricata violentia apprehensi sumus Lucius Montanus Flavianus Iulianus Victoricus Primolus Renus et Donatianus catecuminus, qui baptizatus in carcere statim spiritum reddidit, ab aquae baptismo ad martyrii coronam immaculato itinere festinans. nec non et circa Primolum similis consummationis exitus contigit; nam et ipsum ante paucos menses habita confessio baptizavit.
pass_a_gloss: And for us there is a striving in your sight, most-loved brothers, that you should declare nothing else is to be done by the servants of God and his Christ except to be thinking about the crowd of brothers; by what force, by what reckoning this love, this duty pushed us to this letter, that for brothers who will be hereafter we might leave behind both a faithful witness of God's greatness and a remembrance of our toils and endurance for the Lord. After the mob-uproar which the savage face of the governor roused toward slaughter, and after the very sharp persecution of Christians on the following day, with violence having overstepped bounds, we were seized — Lucius, Montanus, Flavianus, Iulianus, Victoricus, Primolus, Renus and Donatianus a catechumen, who having been baptized in prison immediately gave back his spirit, hurrying from the baptism of water to the crown of martyrdom by a stainless road. And also in the case of Primolus a like end of consummation happened; for him too a confession held a few months before baptized him.
pass_b_english: Beloved brothers, we too are engaged in a contest before you, that you may affirm that nothing else befits the servants of God and of his Christ except to keep the multitude of the brethren in mind; it is the force and the reasoning of this love, this duty, that has compelled us to this letter, so that for the brothers who will come after us we might leave behind both a faithful testimony to the magnificence of God and the memory of our labors and endurance for the Lord.

After the popular riot that the governor's ferocious visage stirred up unto slaughter, and after the fiercest persecution of the Christians on the following day, when violence broke all bounds we were arrested — Lucius, Montanus, Flavianus, Julianus, Victoricus, Primolus, Renus, and Donatianus, still a catechumen, who, baptized in prison, at once yielded up his spirit, hastening from the baptism of water to the crown of martyrdom by an undefiled path.
A like consummation also befell Primolus; for a confession uttered a few months earlier had baptized him also.

lemmas.gloss: unbaptized learner, as spelled in source
gave back, yielded up spirit in death

choices.term: Et nobis est apud vos certamen
choices.english: we too are engaged in a contest before you
choices.why: dative nobis with est gives a task laid on us, and apud vos points to witnesses rather than location, so it is an obligation performed in their sight
ablative absolute with perfect participle describes attendant circumstance of the arrest, and context requires excess rather than legal praevaricatio

choices.english: a confession uttered had baptized him
choices.why: habita with ante paucos menses marks a prior public confession as the effective baptismal act for one who lacked water baptism
